definition: Sensory input is information or feedback entering the nervous system from stimulation of the body’s sensory pathways. In this context, it refers to feedback produced by neuromuscular electrical stimulation that can influence coordination between the motor cortex and spinal motor neurons and affect motor performance.

reasons: The packet supports sensory feedback from neuromuscular electrical stimulation and possible effects on corticomuscular synchronization and motor performance, but it does not support the broader general definition of sensory input as information entering the nervous system from the body's sensory pathways.
The wording shifts from the packet’s cautious “may contribute” and “improvement” to a broader, more categorical explanation of how sensory input works, which is not established by the source text.
